name: McCrae
intro: McCrae sits quietly between Dromana and Rosebud, often skipped over by people who treat the bay drive as a single line  -  which is a shame, because it has the best small-town beach on this stretch and the oldest building still standing on the Peninsula. The McCrae Lighthouse is the postcard, and Andrew McCrae's 1844 homestead, still set in its original garden, is the kind of history that survives only by being mostly forgotten. The foreshore here is a clean, gently shelving bay beach with bathing boxes and a long swimming pier, and the residential streets behind run up to the foot of Arthurs Seat. It is the sort of town that locals on the Peninsula use as a base when Dromana is too busy and Rosebud is too sprawling. Stay here for calm-water swimming and the back-of-Arthurs lookout walks; do not come for nightlife.
factualLede: McCrae is a small bayside town on the Mornington Peninsula's Port Phillip coast between Dromana and Rosebud, 75 km from Melbourne, anchored by McCrae Lighthouse, McCrae Homestead and a calm bayside swimming beach.

heroImage.alt: McCrae Lighthouse above a calm Port Phillip Bay morning

tldr: McCrae is the in-between bay town most visitors skip — calm beach, the Peninsula's oldest homestead, a lighthouse, and the back of Arthurs Seat right behind.
Best for: families wanting calmer bay swimming than Dromana; history-minded travellers; walkers using the Arthurs Seat trails.
Signature experience: morning swim from the bathing boxes, a wander through McCrae Homestead garden, lighthouse photo at dusk.
A weekend works well; pair with Dromana or Rosebud for dining.
Quieter at the foreshore than its neighbours, especially out of school holidays.
notFor: anyone chasing a busy restaurant strip
signature: Bayside swimming, a lighthouse, and the Peninsula's oldest homestead — the bay's quiet middle.
skip: Driving past on the way to Sorrento — McCrae rewards stopping properly.
bestDay: Bayside swim at the bathing boxes, breakfast in Dromana, McCrae Homestead garden mid-morning, Arthurs Seat chairlift up after lunch, lighthouse at golden hour.
insiderNote: Park at the homestead and walk the residential streets down to the lighthouse — the most pleasant approach, and you avoid the foreshore car-park scramble.
